picks.intervention_label: Active surveillance — structured cross-sectional imaging q3-6 months for 2-3 years then space out; no adjuvant systemic therapy
picks.rationale: With no measurable disease and a tumor this indolent, there is nothing for an adjuvant regimen to act on, so the tolerability side of the patient's 0.65 weight wins by default. Boikos 2016 puts imatinib at a 2% response rate in this subset, and both NCCN and ESMO say it plainly: no adjuvant TKI here. Surveillance also keeps every recurrence contingency open instead of spending trial-screening eligibility on a regimen the biology rejects. The one axis it does not fully satisfy is prefers_trials, since surveillance is not a trial, which is exactly why the registry sits right behind it.
primary_concerns: efficacy/tox weight 0.65: satisfied — no chronic toxicity committed where there is no efficacy to gain
prefers_trials: in tension — surveillance is not a trial; the registry pick is the mitigation
no toxicity vetoes or modality constraints were stated, so there is nothing to clear on those axes

picks.intervention_label: NCI Rare Tumor Natural History Study (NCT03739827) + cancer-genetics counseling for the SDHA germline result and POLE R1679C reclassification
picks.rationale: This is the one move that honors prefers_trials today. The patient is NED, which locks them out of nearly every contingency trial that needs measurable disease, but the NCI Rare Tumor Natural History Study takes them as they are, at zero toxicity. It also banks tissue, opens the SDHC-methylation fallback if the SDHA workup wobbles, and pairs cleanly with the genetics counseling the germline question already demands. For a trial-preferring patient with nothing to enroll on, this is as close as it gets right now.
primary_concerns: prefers_trials: fully satisfied — the only enrollable trial while the patient is NED
efficacy/tox weight: satisfied — zero toxicity
preferences are defaulted, not elicited; travel tolerance for the NIH baseline visit should be confirmed before this is leaned on

picks.intervention_label: SDHA germline panel + SDHA/SDHB IHC re-cut with internal control + tumor-tissue NGS confirmation of the ctDNA-only variants
picks.rationale: Every dSDH-GIST trial the patient might want later gates on SDHB-IHC loss, and the report has SDHB reading intact against a biallelic SDHA call, and that discrepancy could quietly disqualify them at screening. One tissue pull answers three things: germline versus somatic SDHA (cascade testing and lifelong PGL surveillance ride on it), whether the SDHA IHC reconciles the paradox, and whether the ctDNA-only variants are real in tumor. There is no therapeutic toxicity, and it protects the trial eligibility the patient says they want. The cost is a few weeks of turnaround before any recurrence plan can move.
primary_concerns: prefers_trials: protected — confirms the SDHB-loss phenotype every contingency trial screens on
efficacy/tox weight: neutral — diagnostic, no therapeutic effect
tension: if the SDHA IHC also reads intact, the dSDH label collapses and the trial route narrows

picks.intervention_label: Paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma baseline surveillance — plasma free metanephrines (LC-MS/MS) + rapid-sequence whole-body MRI; Ga-68 DOTATATE PET/CT reserved for baseline + change-flagging
picks.rationale: An SDHx carrier with an undetected functional paraganglioma who goes under anesthesia for a future re-resection is a hypertensive crisis waiting to happen, and this patient may well face more surgery. One plasma metanephrines draw plus a whole-body MRI sets the clean baseline now, so later the question becomes what changed rather than whether a comparator exists. It is non-invasive, carries no therapeutic toxicity, and runs into no stated preference. Cadence tightens or relaxes once the germline SDHA result is back.
primary_concerns: efficacy/tox weight: satisfied — non-invasive, no therapeutic toxicity
no preference conflict elicited or apparent
annual-versus-biennial cadence is unresolved until the germline result returns

picks.intervention_label: Signatera tumor-informed ctDNA MRD assay as a recurrence-surveillance adjunct to imaging (informative, not therapy-triggering)
picks.rationale: The patient has detectable SDHA, PIK3CA, and MAP2K1 variants in plasma pre-resection, so a tumor-informed assay is genuinely informative for this individual rather than a generic add-on. Signatera can give lead-time over imaging, with one hard guardrail: a positive result buys a shorter-interval scan, not a TKI. It is venipuncture only, so it sits fine against the tolerability weight. The GIST-specific validation is thinner than colorectal or lung, so I would frame it as informative, not therapy-triggering.
primary_concerns: efficacy/tox weight: satisfied — venipuncture only
prefers_trials: partial — an adjunct to a trial-aware plan, not itself a trial
a ctDNA-positive / imaging-negative result is a counseling trap; the imaging guardrail is load-bearing

picks.intervention_label: Recurrence contingency — trial-route first (olverembatinib NCT06640361, belzutifan NCT04924075, pemigatinib/PEMIGIST NCT07434843, temozolomide NCT05661643) with sunitinib as the FDA-approved co-equal fallback
picks.rationale: At first measurable recurrence, prefers_trials says the trial menu gets presented alongside sunitinib, not behind it. The freshest data back that: olverembatinib now has a real dSDH-GIST readout (ORR 23.1%, mPFS 25.7 mo) and is recruiting, belzutifan carries the cleanest mechanism case with 14 US sites open, and pemigatinib rides the rogaratinib signal (ORR 41.7%), though rogaratinib's own trial has closed to accrual, so that specific door is shut. Sunitinib stays the FDA-approved fallback (Boikos 18% ORR in this subset), best offered as a co-equal option rather than the default first reach. Which trial actually fits turns on geography and the dSDH confirmation, neither of which has been elicited yet.
primary_concerns: prefers_trials: satisfied at recurrence — the trial menu is presented alongside, not behind, sunitinib
efficacy/tox weight 0.65: mostly satisfied — oral agents, but real chronic AE profiles (belzutifan anemia compounded by Roux-en-Y; FGFR-class retinal and phosphate monitoring)
tension: geography and dSDH confirmation are unelicited and gate which trial is reachable

picks.intervention_label: Adjuvant imatinib — NOT RECOMMENDED in dSDH-GIST (logged as a veto so the no-imatinib call is documented and not re-litigated)
picks.rationale: I am logging this as a veto so the reflex GIST-means-imatinib reach gets documented and is not re-litigated on the post-op note. In this subset imatinib runs a 2% response rate (Boikos 2016) and ESMO 2022 recommends against it outright. Three years of edema, fatigue, and monitoring burden against a 2% return fails the tolerability weight under any reading, and it would spend the screening eligibility for the contingency trials the patient prefers. With no efficacy to lean on, there is no version of the 0.65 weight that rescues this.
primary_concerns: efficacy/tox weight: fails outright — 2% response against three years of toxicity
prefers_trials: fails — not a trial, and it burns trial-screening eligibility
logged as a veto on the patient's behalf

notes: Worth saying plainly: this patient gave no preferences, so everything above runs on defaults. The 0.65 weight and prefers_trials=true are reasonable stand-ins, but I would want both confirmed before any of this hardens, especially scan-anxiety tolerance (the real cost of indefinite surveillance, and nobody has asked) and travel range (which decides whether the registry visit and the recurrence trials are even reachable). The defaults happen to land on the same answer the guidelines give, but that is convergence, not elicitation.

picks.intervention_label: active surveillance (guideline-aligned default; no adjuvant TKI)
picks.rationale: ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS GIST CPG 2022 and NCCN GIST v1.2026 converge on the same answer for this subtype: no adjuvant TKI, surveillance instead. ESMO 2022 states the consensus plainly, that adjuvant treatment is avoided in SDH-expression-negative GISTs, because they do not respond to imatinib and tend to run an indolent course. The natural-history data favor an imaging plan over a drug: recurrence is the rule in dSDH-GIST (~71% eventually recur or progress, median EFS ~2.5 yr post-resection), yet no adjuvant agent has been shown to bend that curve. This is the guideline default and I rank it first without hedging.
primary_concerns: SDHB IHC currently reads intact, which sits oddly against two somatic SDHA hits at ~85% combined VAF; the re-cut the profile flags has to confirm the SDH-deficient phenotype before the ESMO avoid-adjuvant consensus formally attaches to this patient.
Germline SDHA is still pending. Resolving it is itself a guideline step (NCCN GIST v1.2026 directs genetic-counseling referral for all SDH-deficient GIST), not an optional extra.

picks.intervention_label: NCI Rare Tumor Natural History Study + genetic-counseling referral (NCT03739827)
picks.rationale: NCCN GIST v1.2026 recommends genetic-counseling and germline-testing referral for every SDH-deficient GIST, and this is the route that operationalizes it. The NCI Rare Tumor Natural History Study (NCT03739827) takes SDH-deficient GIST regardless of disease status, so the NED setting is not a blocker, and it plugs the patient into the NIH Pediatric and wt-GIST referral network where the SDHA and SDHB workup actually gets settled. It satisfies the guideline and the stated trial preference at once, without committing to any unproven systemic agent.
primary_concerns: This is a natural-history and biospecimen protocol, not a therapeutic one; the value is diagnostic resolution and specialist access, not disease control.
Enrollment leans on NIH-site evaluation, which carries a travel ask on top of community-based imaging.

picks.intervention_label: sunitinib (guideline-preferred 2L TKI at first recurrence)
picks.rationale: When measurable disease returns, the guideline-endorsed first systemic move in this subtype is sunitinib, not imatinib. NCCN GIST v1.2026 carries sunitinib as a second-line option, and for SDH-deficient disease specifically the NIH cohort (Boikos 2016) reports objective response 7/38 (18%) on sunitinib versus 1/49 (2%) on imatinib, which is the published basis ESMO 2022 cites for preferring it here. The effect is modest, but it is the consensus opening move for the contingency plan.
primary_concerns: The Boikos response figures are retrospective with small per-drug n; activity in dSDH-GIST is genuine but lower than in KIT-mutant disease.
Not applicable while the patient is NED. This is a contingency anchor for first recurrence, not an action for now.

picks.intervention_label: regorafenib (guideline-sequenced 3L TKI)
picks.rationale: NCCN GIST v1.2026 and ESMO 2022 sequence regorafenib after sunitinib, on the GRID pivotal RCT. dSDH-GIST was under-represented in GRID, so subset activity is extrapolation, characterized as modest in the von Mehren 2025 review rather than demonstrated in a dedicated dSDH cohort. It earns its place as the guideline-aligned third-line rung of the contingency ladder, with the evidence caveat stated up front.
primary_concerns: No dSDH-GIST-specific trial data; the subset claim rests on extrapolation from a KIT-mutant-dominated pivotal trial.
Contingency only, and only after sunitinib in the guideline sequence.

picks.intervention_label: clinical-trial enrollment at recurrence: SDH-deficient temozolomide cohort (NCT05661643)
picks.rationale: This is where guideline and preference line up: NCCN GIST v1.2026 explicitly prefers clinical-trial enrollment for SDH-deficient and wt-GIST, so at recurrence a trial is the endorsed path rather than a detour. The SDH-deficient temozolomide cohort (NCT05661643) is the cleanest indication match and rides single-arm phase-2 activity specific to this subtype (~40% response, Burgoyne case series). I am ranking the trial route, not temozolomide as a standard, because the drug itself is not yet guideline-endorsed.
primary_concerns: Temozolomide is off-guideline as a standard agent; the guideline-fit here is the trial-enrollment route, not the drug.
The trial requires measurable disease, so it excludes the current NED state, and NCT05661643 runs out of Asan Medical Center in Korea, a real travel constraint.
Promising newer agents in this subtype (olverembatinib, rogaratinib, belzutifan) sit in the same off-guideline trial-territory category until their readouts mature.

notes: Anchored to ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS GIST CPG 2022 and NCCN GIST v1.2026. The decisive call is that adjuvant imatinib is off-guideline for this patient: ESMO 2022 puts SDH-expression-negative GIST in the avoid-adjuvant column, and the registration RCTs (Z9001, SSGXVIII, PERSIST-5) either excluded or separated out the imatinib-insensitive genotypes this patient belongs to. If the board hears 'why not 3 years of adjuvant imatinib,' the guideline answer is that the subset was never shown to benefit and does not respond. Everything past rank 2 is contingency framing for first recurrence; nothing systemic is indicated while NED. All of it is provisional on the SDHB re-cut and germline SDHA resolution confirming the dSDH phenotype the whole plan rests on.

picks.intervention_label: Active surveillance + NCI rare-tumor natural-history registry
picks.rationale: This patient is NED after an R0 resection that also cleared the single M1 deposit, and dSDH-GIST runs indolent, so the bar for committing to chronic-toxicity systemic therapy is high and nothing in the dossier clears it. Adjuvant imatinib is the one regimen with decade-long safety follow-up (SSGXVIII 10-year data), but it does not transport: dSDH-GIST was never enrolled in those trials and imatinib managed 1/49 (2%) responses in this subtype (Boikos 2016), so the toxicity would buy almost no benefit. Structured surveillance carries no treatment toxicity at all, and the natural history is clear enough to plan around, with median EFS ~2.5 yr post-resection and recurrence or progression in ~71% (Mei 2018), which argues for biennial whole-body MRI plus paraganglioma screening rather than a drug. Enroll on the NCI rare-tumor natural-history registry (NCT03739827, open regardless of disease status) and resolve germline-vs-somatic SDHA for counseling while we watch.
primary_concerns: Recurrence is the expectation here, not the exception, so the surveillance schedule has to actually run on time or the indolence argument stops protecting the patient.
SDHB IHC currently reads intact against two SDHA somatic hits; the re-cut needs to happen now, because it gates every contingency trial downstream.

picks.intervention_label: sunitinib
picks.rationale: At first recurrence with measurable disease, sunitinib is the best-characterized systemic option on the table: FDA-approved since 2006, anchored by a placebo-controlled phase 3 (TTP HR 0.33, p<0.0001; Demetri 2006) and roughly two decades of post-marketing safety, so its AEs (fatigue, diarrhea, hand-foot reaction, skin discoloration, hypertension) come with well-worn management algorithms. The dSDH-specific efficacy is modest but genuine, and this is the published preferred 2L TKI here, with 7/38 (18%) objective responses versus imatinib's 2% (Boikos 2016). I am not overselling it; the response rate sits below the newer FGFR and multikinase agents. What it offers is a predictable toxicity tail, which matters most when the alternative is an indolent tumor and an unfamiliar safety profile.
primary_concerns: 18% ORR is honest but unimpressive; if the recurrence is bulky or fast-moving, a more active agent may be worth a less-charted safety profile.
Hypertension and hand-foot reaction need baseline BP and skin monitoring built in from cycle 1.

picks.intervention_label: temozolomide
picks.rationale: Temozolomide is a decades-old alkylator with a thoroughly mapped, predictable toxicity profile, mostly myelosuppression, fatigue, and nausea, all with standard dose-modification and antiemetic algorithms, so the safety side is well understood even though the dSDH efficacy base is thin (2/5 PR, 40% ORR; Yebra 2022). The reason it ranks here rather than lower is that the benefit is biomarker-selectable: MGMT promoter methylation sits in ~24% (8/33) of dSDH-GIST and predicts the alkylator response (Giger 2022, Flego 2024). I would gate any TMZ commitment on MGMT methylation testing first, which keeps us from pushing an unselected patient through avoidable cytopenias. An enrolling trial exists (NCT05661643) and satisfies the trial preference, though it is Korea-based and requires measurable disease.
primary_concerns: Myelosuppression is the predictable cost; without MGMT methylation the expected benefit may not justify the cytopenias.
n=5 is the entire prospective efficacy base in this subtype, so the 40% ORR is fragile.

picks.intervention_label: olverembatinib
picks.rationale: Among the newer agents, olverembatinib is the one with a usable safety table: in the 66-patient phase 1b, grade >=3 treatment-related AEs ran 13.6% with zero AE-related discontinuations, and the events (cytopenias, transaminase rise, hyperuricemia) are familiar and monitorable (Qiu 2025). The dSDH efficacy is meaningful for this hard subtype, 6/26 (23.1%) PR with mPFS 25.7 mo. I rank it below the established agents because the evidence is single-arm phase 1b, not the long post-marketing record I prefer, and two access problems are real: the sponsor and the registrational phase 3 (NCT06640361) sit in China, and that trial's SDHB-IHC-loss entry criterion conflicts with this patient's currently intact SDHB stain until the re-cut resolves it.
primary_concerns: Phase 1b with n=26 in-subtype; the 25.7-mo PFS could shrink in a randomized setting.
Access and the SDHB-IHC entry mismatch may keep this academic unless the re-stain confirms loss.

picks.intervention_label: rogaratinib
picks.rationale: Rogaratinib has the strongest efficacy signal in dSDH-GIST anyone has published, 10/24 (41.7%) PR and mPFS 31.0 mo (Merriam 2026), and the FGFR mechanism is well-grounded preclinically. My objection is specific and it is a safety objection: the per-grade AE distribution is not retrievable. The abstract names only hyperphosphatemia, fatigue, and diarrhea with no grades, CT.gov posts no AE table, and the full text is paywalled, so I cannot characterize the toxicity I would be signing this patient up for. The trial is also closed to accrual, so even setting the safety gap aside this is a watch-for-the-paper option, not an actionable one today.
primary_concerns: Hyperphosphatemia is the known pan-FGFR class effect and needs phosphate monitoring plus a binder plan, but the grade distribution in this cohort is unpublished.
Closed to accrual; there is no access path right now even if the efficacy holds up.

notes: The honest summary: there is no adjuvant move here I can defend on safety grounds, because the only regimen with long follow-up (imatinib) is the one that does not work in this genotype. So the conservative position is a plan, not a prescription: disciplined surveillance plus a pre-agreed contingency ladder. Order of preference at recurrence tracks how well I can predict the toxicity, not just the ORR, so sunitinib first, MGMT-gated TMZ next, then the newer agents once their safety tables and access firm up. The SDHB re-cut is load-bearing for half of these options and should happen now, not at recurrence.

picks.intervention_label: Active surveillance (no adjuvant systemic therapy); structured cross-sectional imaging q3-6 months for 2-3 years, then space out
picks.rationale: The adjuvant decision is the one place in this dossier where the high-quality evidence points somewhere, and it points away from drugs. The registration-grade adjuvant-imatinib RCTs (Z9001; SSGXVIII at 10 years; PERSIST-5; all RoB2 Low) enrolled KIT-driven disease and structurally excluded SDH-deficient GIST, and ESMO recommends against imatinib here because Boikos 2016 saw 1/49 (2%) responses in this subset. No RCT, and no single-arm trial, supports any adjuvant systemic therapy in dSDH-GIST. Recurrence is common (Mei 2018: ~71%, median EFS 2.5 yr) but the biology is indolent, so structured imaging beats committing an NED patient to chronic toxicity with zero supporting trial.
primary_concerns: Indirectness: the adjuvant RCTs that justify withholding treatment come from a KIT-mutant population, so the no-adjuvant call here is an absence-of-evidence inference rather than a trial-tested one.

The natural-history recurrence figures (Mei 2018) come from a narrative review citing a retrospective surgical cohort (tier 5, ROBINS-I not gradable); fine for framing surveillance intensity, not for hard risk quantitation.

picks.intervention_label: Confirm the molecular foundation: SDHB/SDHA IHC re-cut with internal control, SDHA germline-vs-somatic panel, tumor-tissue NGS confirmation of the ctDNA-only variants
picks.rationale: Before any molecular rationale earns a vote, the molecular calls have to hold. SDHB IHC reads intact while two somatic SDHA variants sit at roughly 85% combined VAF, and biallelic SDHA inactivation should collapse the complex and wipe out SDHB staining, so the discordance needs a re-cut with a positive internal control before the dSDH label is load-bearing. The PIK3CA R93W, MAP2K1 P124S, and SDHA E350fs calls are ctDNA-only and unconfirmed in tissue, and R93W sits outside the alpelisib/inavolisib companion-diagnostic hotspots. One tissue pull resolves the driver call, the germline-vs-somatic SDHA question, and the eligibility gate for every recurrence trial downstream.
primary_concerns: Measurement/classification risk: SDHB-IHC intact against biallelic SDHA is an internal contradiction; accepting the current stain risks misclassifying the driver.

ctDNA-only variant calls carry clonal-hematopoiesis and assay-artifact risk with no orthogonal tissue confirmation yet; R93W and P124S in particular should not gate any therapy until tissue confirms them.

picks.intervention_label: Sunitinib 50 mg PO 4-on/2-off (or 37.5 mg continuous) at first measurable recurrence; NOT adjuvant
picks.rationale: At measurable recurrence, sunitinib is the best-evidenced systemic option here, which is a low bar met rather than a strong endorsement. Its own pivotal is RCT-grade (Demetri 2006, n=312, TTP HR 0.33, p<0.0001, RoB2 Low) but did not stratify SDH status and was overwhelmingly KIT-mutant, so the subtype-specific claim rests on Boikos 2016: 7/38 (18%) SDH-deficient responders on sunitinib vs 1/49 (2%) on imatinib, retrospective and ROBINS-I Moderate. Read the 18% as directional, not as a dependable response estimate. It edges out regorafenib and ripretinib only because their dSDH evidence base is thinner still.
primary_concerns: Indirectness: the pivotal RCT population was KIT-mutant with no SDH stratification, so the HR 0.33 does not transport cleanly to this subtype.
Boikos 2016 is retrospective (ROBINS-I Moderate) with small per-drug n and no per-AE capture; selection and confounding risk sit inside the 18% response figure.

picks.intervention_label: Rogaratinib (pan-FGFR1-4 inhibitor) at recurrence, trial route only (NCI cohort closed; FGFR-pathway evidence anchor)
picks.rationale: Rogaratinib has the highest ORR reported for any systemic agent in this subtype, 10/24 (41.7%) PR with mPFS 31.0 mo (95% CI 20.2-NR), in the exact molecular population. That is a real signal worth a trial referral, but it comes from one single-arm, open-label phase 2 of n=24 with no comparator and an ORR endpoint, and per-term AE rates I cannot verify: the abstract names only hyperphosphatemia, fatigue, and diarrhea, the CT.gov results tab is empty, and the full text is paywalled. The cohort enrolled regardless of FGFR status, so the response is not anchored to a predictive biomarker. It is unreplicated; the confirmatory pemigatinib trial (NCT07434843) has not read out, and rogaratinib's own cohort is closed to accrual.
primary_concerns: Single-arm open-label ORR endpoint: no comparator and unblinded response ascertainment, with a real risk that dSDH indolence inflates the 50% SD fraction in the 91.7% DCR.

Selective/incomplete outcome reporting: per-term AE data are not retrievable from abstract, CT.gov, or the paywalled full text, so the safety profile is unverified (I read the abstract and the structured row, not the full paper).
No replication; the FGFR rationale rests on the Flavahan FGF4-insulator mechanism, which is mechanistic plausibility rather than clinical confirmation.

picks.intervention_label: Olverembatinib (multikinase TKI) at recurrence, trial route only (phase 1b signal; phase-3 NCT06640361 watch)
picks.rationale: Olverembatinib shows 6/26 (23.1%, 95% CI 9-43.7) PR and mPFS 25.7 mo, but the design is a single-arm phase 1b expansion of n=26 inside a 66-patient basket, and the safety table is pooled across all 66 rather than the GIST cohort. The mechanism is non-canonical for a KIT/PDGFRA-WT tumor: this is a KIT/ABL TKI acting through VEGFR/FGFR/HIF-CD36 axes, not its labeled target, so plausibility is borrowed rather than demonstrated in-indication. The NCT06640361 'phase 3' is phase-3 in name only, being open-label, single intervention, no comparator arm, n=40, with a PFS-rate endpoint. That design will not deliver randomized evidence, and the SDHB-IHC-loss entry criterion is one this patient does not currently meet.
primary_concerns: Single-arm phase 1b with an ORR endpoint; safety pooled across the 66-patient basket rather than the n=26 GIST cohort, so subtype-specific tolerability is unresolved.
The confirmatory NCT06640361 is labeled phase 3 but is single-arm/no-comparator with a PFS-rate surrogate, so it will not generate RCT-grade evidence.
Non-canonical MoA in a KIT-WT tumor: the efficacy claim cannot lean on the labeled target.

picks.intervention_label: Temozolomide with MGMT-methylation enrichment, trial route only; late contingency at recurrence
picks.rationale: Temozolomide is a contingency, not a recommendation, and the evidence is thin enough that I would only run it on a trial with MGMT enrichment. The clinical anchor is Yebra 2022: 2/5 (40%) PR in SDH-mutant GIST, which is n=5, a translational case series, ROBINS-I Serious, tier 4, with no per-AE table. The one biomarker lever is real (Giger 2022: MGMT promoter hypermethylation in 8/33 (24%) SDH-deficient tumors and 0% elsewhere), so methylation testing could enrich for the likely responders before exposing anyone to an alkylator. A 5-patient series is hypothesis-generating; it does not support TMZ as a default off-label move.
primary_concerns: n=5 case series, ROBINS-I Serious, tier 4: severe small-sample and selection bias, with a 40% ORR whose confidence interval is wide enough to be uninformative.
No per-AE safety table in the source, so toxicity in this exact population is uncharacterized.
The MGMT-methylation predictive value (Giger 2022) is a retrospective biomarker association, not validated as a treatment-selection marker in a prospective trial.

notes: Not abstaining: for the adjuvant question the high-quality evidence is unusually clear and supports surveillance, so I have a confident rank 1 for once. Three mechanism-matched strategies are already closed by negative subtype-specific trials and I ranked none of them: guadecitabine 0/9 (Ligon 2023, terminated for accrual), linsitinib 0/20 (von Mehren 2020), vandetanib 0/9 (Glod 2019); their 'stable disease' fractions most plausibly reflect dSDH indolence rather than drug effect, which is also the main reason I discount the single-arm DCR figures for rogaratinib and olverembatinib. I deliberately ranked no PI3Kalpha (alpelisib/inavolisib/RLY-2608) or MEK (trametinib) option: R93W and P124S are ctDNA-only and non-canonical, the registration data are breast-cancer cross-tumor, and the trametinib MAP2K1 precedent is cross-tumor and cross-class. POLE R1679C with TMB<1 and MSS gives no ICI rationale; that is a genetic-counseling item, not a therapy. For rogaratinib and olverembatinib I read the abstracts plus the structured rows, not the full texts, so my AE-completeness criticisms are bounded by that.

picks.intervention_label: rogaratinib (pan-FGFR1-4 inhibitor)
picks.rationale: The biggest swing on the board. Rogaratinib posted ORR 41.7% (10/24) and mPFS 31.0 mo in dSDH-GIST (PMID 42191879), the best numbers any systemic agent has put up in this subtype, and the FGF4-insulator mechanism is backed by a PDX that responded where sunitinib and regorafenib did nothing (Flavahan 2019, Flynn 2025 CT215). The catch is real: n=24 single-arm, and NCT04595747 is closed to accrual with Bayer off the program, so getting the actual drug is the hard part. If disease comes back, I want this pathway hit first.
primary_concerns: NCT04595747 is closed to accrual and Bayer has stepped back from rogaratinib, so access likely means compassionate use rather than enrollment
Single-arm n=24 with no comparator; 41.7% could shrink in a broader or less-selected population
Pan-FGFR hyperphosphatemia needs monitoring, though it tracked target engagement rather than capping the dose

picks.intervention_label: pemigatinib (FGFR1-3 inhibitor)
picks.rationale: Same FGFR pathway, but with a door that is actually open. NCT07434843 (George/DFCI, recruiting) runs in this exact subtype, and the patient wants trials, so this is how I would cash the FGFR bet if rogaratinib stays unreachable. The PDX work hit tumors with pemigatinib too, not only rogaratinib (Flynn 2025 CT215), so the pathway logic carries across the two agents. The honest gap is no clinical readout yet, and it is another 24-patient single-arm design.
primary_concerns: No clinical efficacy data in dSDH-GIST yet; the bet rides on the rogaratinib readout plus the shared PDX response
Requires measurable disease, so it is a recurrence option, not something to start now
FGFR class hyperphosphatemia and a day 1-14 of 21 schedule to manage

picks.intervention_label: olverembatinib (HQP1351, multikinase inhibitor)
picks.rationale: A durable-control play with the cleanest safety sheet in the dossier. 6/26 confirmed PR (ORR 23.1%) and mPFS 25.7 mo, with grade 3+ events in only 13.6% and zero discontinuations across the phase 1b (PMID 41184234), and it has already moved into phase 3 (NCT06640361). For a patient in their 40s who may be on therapy for years, that tolerability weighs almost as much as the response rate. Two blockers I will not paper over: the phase 3 requires SDHB-IHC loss, which this patient's stain does not currently show pending the re-cut, and the sponsor sits in China.
primary_concerns: Phase 3 entry requires SDHB-IHC loss; the patient's SDHB reads intact and needs re-stain before the dSDH label and eligibility hold
Ascentage sponsorship in China makes access a separate problem from eligibility
ORR 23.1% is roughly half the rogaratinib signal

picks.intervention_label: temozolomide (MGMT-methylation-dependent alkylator)
picks.rationale: If the tumor is MGMT-methylated, this could be the highest-yield oral option on the list. The Yebra series hit 40% ORR (2/5) with 100% disease control (PMID 34426440), the patient-derived models showed on-target killing while imatinib, sunitinib and regorafenib did nothing, and about 24% of dSDH-GIST carry the MGMT methylation that predicts response (PMID 36198483). Order the MGMT test now; if it reads methylated, I would push hard for the recruiting NCT05661643 at recurrence. The honest weakness is n=5, the patient's MGMT status is unknown, and most dSDH tumors are unmethylated, so this is biomarker-gated rather than a sure thing.
primary_concerns: MGMT methylation status unknown; only ~24% of dSDH-GIST are methylated, so the predictive biomarker may not flag
Clinical signal rests on a 5-patient series
The enrolling trial NCT05661643 is in Korea, so travel feasibility is a real constraint

picks.intervention_label: belzutifan (HIF-2alpha inhibitor)
picks.rationale: The most direct shot at the actual driver. Belzutifan blocks HIF-2alpha, the node that succinate accumulation stabilizes in precisely this biology (Selak 2005 PMID 15652751; Bayley 2022 SDHB model PMID 35324464), and the PPGL cohort of LITESPARK-015 already showed ORR 26% with mPFS 22 mo in a sibling SDH-loss disease. Because it is approved off-label, access does not hinge on enrollment, which is rare among these options. What I cannot claim is a GIST readout: the wt-GIST cohort of NCT04924075 has not reported, so this is mechanism plus cross-indication signal and nothing firmer.
primary_concerns: No published dSDH-GIST efficacy; the case rests on mechanism and the PPGL cohort
Anemia and fatigue are expected HIF-2alpha class effects
Guadecitabine, another mechanistically-matched agent, returned 0/9 in this subtype (PMID 36302175), a reminder that target validation does not guarantee a clinical response

notes: Framing matters here. The patient is NED after R0 resection of multifocal disease plus a completely resected M1 deposit, so there is no measurable lesion to enroll on today, and every active option above is a contingency for first recurrence rather than an adjuvant order. I am deliberately not pushing chronic active therapy now: there is no adjuvant evidence in dSDH-GIST (the imatinib adjuvant RCTs structurally excluded this subtype), the tumor is indolent, and dosing a NED patient with FGFR or TKI toxicity is harm without a target. What I would do now is build the contingency stack, get the MGMT test plus the SDHB re-cut and germline SDHA resolution done so eligibility is ready, and enroll in the NCI rare-tumor registry (NCT03739827), which takes patients regardless of disease status. Recurrence is the rule in this subtype (~71%, median EFS ~2.5 yr; PMID 29413424), so the whole bet is to be ready to swing hard the moment disease returns.
